title: Approvals for Hazardous Materials
source_verification_depth: Complete Supporting Statement A plus package; underlying cited sources not all independently retrieved. Specific corroboration recorded separately.

score_rationale.reproducibility: Thirteen application categories expose counts, frequencies and hours; overall products reconstruct.
score_rationale.provenance: 2022 chemical engineer wages and OPM schedule identified; benefit-share vintage and task timing evidence weaker.
score_rationale.segmentation: Initial/renewal applications and approval types distinguished.
score_rationale.labor: Engineer occupation and denominator benefit loading are clear; common share lacks current source detail.
score_rationale.item13: No additional nonlabor costs asserted without further price or systems analysis.
score_rationale.item14: Federal workload and loaded grade rate supplied, but narrative and table use different rates and counts.
score_rationale.item15: Removal of one approval and five rounded hours tied to rule.
score_rationale.validation: Agency experience, without testing or representative timing measurements.
score_rationale.consistency: Item 14 table contains 14894 and 73.23 while prose uses 14893 and 80.48.

assumptions: 13 approval categories; detailed timing assumptions unchanged from prior estimates.

reconstruction_issues: Federal narrative and table mix different workload counts and pay rates, preventing one unambiguous total.
Benefit-share denominator is explicit but source-period linkage is incomplete.
methods_worth_testing: Generate narrative and tables from one scenario to prevent stale federal-cost inputs.
